learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn to use prepositions of direction—such as into, onto, across, through, towards, and along—to accurately describe movement.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Imagine you are a brave explorer drawing a treasure map. To guide someone, you need special words that show movement and direction. Let's learn these magical compass words—Prepositions of Direction! 🧭

lesson_modules.teaching_content: We use 'Into' when someone or something is moving towards the INSIDE of a space. We use 'Onto' when moving to the TOP surface of something. These words show action, unlike 'in' or 'on' which just show resting position.
examples_or_templates: The frog jumped into the pond. (Moving to the inside)
The cat leaped onto the table. (Moving to the top surface)

lesson_modules.module_title: 🌉 Across & Through (Getting to the Other Side)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: We use 'Across' when moving from one side of a surface to the other side. We use 'Through' when moving inside something that has boundaries (like a tunnel, forest, or pipe).
examples_or_templates: We walked across the bridge. (On the surface from side A to B)
The train went through the dark tunnel. (Entering and coming out)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: We use 'Towards' to show the direction of movement (getting closer to something). We use 'Along' when moving beside a line, like a river, a road, or a beach.
examples_or_templates: The dog ran towards me. (In my direction)
We took a walk along the beach. (Following the edge of the water)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which preposition fits best? 'The thief escaped by jumping _______ the window.'
❓ Choose the correct word: 'He dived ______ the swimming pool.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank: 'The cars are driving _______ the long highway.'
subjective_practice.hint: They are moving in a line beside or on the path.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct the sentence: 'The horse jumped in the fence.'
subjective_practice.hint: Did it go inside the fence, or from one side to the other? (Use 'across' or 'over')

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write one sentence using the word 'towards'.
subjective_practice.hint: Think about moving in the direction of a person or a building!

activity_or_assignment.title: 🏰 Obstacle Course Narrator
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Set up a tiny obstacle course with pillows and chairs. Make a toy car or action figure move 'across' a pillow, 'through' a tunnel (under a chair), and 'onto' a book. Speak out loud the prepositions as you move it!

chapter_summary: ⭐ 'Into' and 'Onto' show movement to the inside or the top of something.
⭐ 'Across' means moving over a surface; 'Through' means moving inside a closed space.
⭐ 'Towards' shows movement in a direction, and 'Along' means following a line or path.
